Class InputRouter

java.lang.Object
com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.input.InputRouter
public final class InputRouter extends Object
Routes native events to their windows and lends legacy input APIs a hosted view.

Old Minecraft GUI code reads global Keyboard/Mouse methods. During a hosted action, a temporary WindowBridge answers those reads for the detached window, while preventing that action from draining or grabbing the main window's input. The previous bridge, dimensions, current events, and repeat setting are restored afterward, including when addon code throws.

Scoped operations must run sequentially on the client thread. Nested scopes retain their outer values, but these static markers are not thread-local. The native watcher copies relevant events into each window's synchronized queue; it does not render or invoke GUI callbacks.

  • Constructor Details

    • InputRouter

      public InputRouter(Map<Integer,Window> windows)
      Registers an SDL event watcher for the driver's lifetime. This router is intended to be constructed once; it has no independent shutdown API.
      Parameters:
      windows - live map of native IDs to windows
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if SDL cannot install the watcher

  • Method Details

    • runScoped

      public static void runScoped(Window window, Runnable action)
      Runs client code as though input and display dimensions belonged to one hosted window. The native OS focus is not changed. Focus queries inside the borrowed bridge deliberately report true so ordinary widgets can process the supplied input.
      Parameters:
      window - non-null window supplying held input and drawable dimensions
      action - callback executed immediately; failures propagate after restoration

    • dispatchMouse

      public static <T> T dispatchMouse(int guiX, int guiY, int button, boolean pressed, float wheel, Supplier<T> action)
      Exposes one mouse event while a GUI callback runs, restoring the previous event afterward. GUI coordinates are converted to the bridge's drawable-pixel coordinates when a window scope is active; without a scope they pass through unchanged.

      Supply wheel movement in notches. LWJGLY converts it to legacy units when Mouse.getEventDWheel() is read, using 120 units per notch. Do not multiply the wheel argument by 120 before passing it here.

      Type Parameters:
      T - callback result type
      Parameters:
      guiX - pointer X in scaled GUI units
      guiY - pointer Y in scaled GUI units from the top
      button - Minecraft button index, or a negative value for no button
      pressed - button-down state for this transition
      wheel - vertical wheel movement in notches; zero for ordinary button events
      action - callback querying the synthetic legacy event
      Returns:
      callback result

    • dispatchKey

      public static <T> T dispatchKey(KeyEvent key, Supplier<T> action)
      Exposes a key transition and its modifier snapshot to one GUI callback. Uses SDL identity for the bridge, which translates for the legacy facade. Previous event pointers are restored even if the callback fails.
      Type Parameters:
      T - callback result type
      Parameters:
      key - borrowed event values for this dispatch
      action - callback querying the synthetic legacy key event
      Returns:
      callback result

    • releaseIfOwner

      public void releaseIfOwner(Window window)
      Marks a window unfocused and clears its remembered held keys/buttons. The historical name does not imply a separate owner comparison: this always clears the supplied window, as needed on focus loss or removal.
      Parameters:
      window - window losing input ownership

    • sdlToGuiButton

      public static int sdlToGuiButton(int sdlButton)
      Converts SDL's left/middle/right numbering to Minecraft's left/right/middle order. Extra buttons keep their relative order after converting to zero-based indexing.
      Parameters:
      sdlButton - positive SDL button number
      Returns:
      Minecraft/LWJGL button index
